note: Matched to the ANIMAL rows that already carry descriptions -- Axolotl: 'Refused to grow up. The universe respected this.' Punchy, two or three sentences, one real distinguishing fact each, attitude rather than encyclopedia.

entries.title: Aardvark
entries.description: Digs all night, eats insects by the tens of thousands, and is closely related to nothing you would guess. The nose does most of the work.

entries.title: Albatross
entries.description: Wingspan of a small aircraft. Stays airborne for years at a stretch. Landing is the part they find difficult.

entries.title: Alpaca
entries.description: Fleece worth considerably more than the argument. Will still have the argument.
entries.flavorText: The spitting is a last resort. It is not a rare one.

entries.title: Armadillo
entries.description: Already wearing the armor, so nothing has to be decided in a hurry. Rolls up and simply waits the situation out.

entries.title: Binturong
entries.description: Smells distinctly of hot buttered popcorn and offers no explanation. Prehensile tail. Entirely unbothered.

entries.title: Blobfish
entries.description: Perfectly ordinary at eleven hundred metres down. The famous photograph was taken after decompression, which is nobody's best look.

entries.title: Capybara
entries.description: Gets along with genuinely everything. Birds perch on them, crocodiles decline to escalate, and the secret has never once been shared.

entries.title: Caracal
entries.description: Ear tufts like antennae. Leaps three metres straight up to take birds out of the air, then lands as though nothing happened.

entries.title: Cassowary
entries.description: Closest thing still walking around to a dinosaur, and fully aware of it. The helmet is real, the kick is worse, and the blue is genuinely that blue.

entries.title: Chinchilla
entries.description: Densest fur of any land mammal, which makes water a catastrophe. Bathes in volcanic dust instead and enjoys it enormously.

entries.title: Civet
entries.description: Produces a musk the perfume industry has never quite replaced, and a coffee bean nobody consulted them about.

entries.title: Cockatoo
entries.description: Outlives its owner, dismantles the furniture, and screams at a volume best measured in city blocks. Deeply affectionate throughout.

entries.title: Cuttlefish
entries.description: Changes colour faster than thought, in patterns it cannot itself see, because it is colourblind. Solves this anyway.

entries.title: Dingo
entries.description: Not quite a dog and definitively not a pet. Made that choice a very long time ago and has not revisited it.

entries.title: Dolphin
entries.description: Calls the others by name. Solves problems nobody set. Has a cruel streak that everyone politely leaves out of the brochure.

entries.title: Dugong
entries.description: Mistaken for a mermaid by sailors, which says more about voyage length than about the dugong. Eats seagrass. Wants nothing.

entries.title: Echidna
entries.description: Lays eggs, carries spines, detects electricity through its snout, and is a mammal the entire time. Nobody has explained this satisfactorily.

entries.title: Emu
entries.description: Flightless, fast, and historically undefeated in open conflict with the Australian army. That is a matter of record rather than a joke.

entries.title: Ermine
entries.description: Turns white for winter and keeps the black tail tip. Royalty put it on ceremonial robes; the stoat carried on killing things twice its size.

entries.title: Firefly
entries.description: The light is a sentence. Every species keeps its own rhythm, and a few of them use it to lie to each other.

entries.title: Flamingo
entries.description: Pink entirely on account of what it eats. Stands on one leg because it is easier that way, not to make a point.

entries.title: Gerbil
entries.description: Desert engineering in a very small package. Drinks almost nothing, digs constantly, and thumps a warning most of the room cannot hear.

entries.title: Gharial
entries.description: A crocodilian that specialised entirely in fish and grew a snout like a pair of forceps. Harmless to you. Devastating if you swim.

entries.title: Glowworm
entries.description: Hangs sticky threads from a cave ceiling and glows to draw things upward. Those stars are a trap and always were.

entries.title: Hedgehog
entries.description: Curls into a decision nobody can argue with. Covers surprising distances after dark. Cannot process milk, whatever the storybooks claim.

entries.title: Hoatzin
entries.description: Ferments leaves in a crop the way a cow would and smells accordingly. Its chicks have claws on their wings for climbing back up.

entries.title: Iguana
entries.description: Runs on borrowed sunlight and detaches its tail the moment a conversation turns physical. Grows a replacement, slightly less impressive.

entries.title: Kingfisher
entries.description: Enters water without a splash, which is precisely why the bullet train has that nose. Sits perfectly still until the instant it does not.

entries.title: Kinkajou
entries.description: Prehensile tail, nocturnal habits, and a tongue built for raiding flowers and beehives. Related to raccoons, which explains a great deal.

entries.title: Koala
entries.description: Sleeps twenty hours because the diet affords nothing more. Its fingerprints are indistinguishable from a human's and have genuinely confused investigations.

entries.title: Kudu
entries.description: Spiral horns that take years to finish, and a stillness that makes a very large animal disappear in open scrub.

entries.title: Llama
entries.description: Carries the load and guards the flock. Spits with real precision the moment the arrangement is questioned.

entries.title: Loon
entries.description: The call carries the length of a lake and unsettles everyone who hears it. Solid bones rather than hollow ones, which is what lets it sink and hunt.

entries.title: Lynx
entries.description: Paws built like snowshoes and ear tufts that do something for the hearing. Has followed the hare population up and down for its entire history.

entries.title: Manatee
entries.description: Moves at the speed of a decision nobody is rushing. Eats a tenth of its own weight in seagrass and has no natural enemy except boats.

entries.title: Mandrill
entries.description: The largest monkey there is, wearing the most saturated face in the mammal kingdom. The colour intensifies with rank.

entries.title: Marmoset
entries.description: Small enough to sit in a palm, with teeth built for gouging trees and drinking whatever comes out. Almost always arrives as twins.

entries.title: Meerkat
entries.description: Somebody is always on watch and the shift rotates. That upright posture is a job rather than a personality.

entries.title: Mink
entries.description: Semiaquatic, short-tempered, and historically valued for entirely the wrong reason. Superb swimmer regardless of anyone's opinion.

entries.title: Mongoose
entries.description: Resistant to venom that would end anything its size, and quick enough not to need the resistance. Uses it regardless.

entries.title: Mudskipper
entries.description: A fish that got out and stayed out. Breathes through its skin, walks on its fins, and defends a mud puddle like sovereign territory.

entries.title: Narwhal
entries.description: The tusk is a tooth, spiralled, packed with nerves, and still not fully accounted for. Everyone has a theory and none of them agree.

entries.title: Numbat
entries.description: Puts away twenty thousand termites a day with a tongue longer than seems reasonable. One of very few marsupials awake in daylight.

entries.title: Okapi
entries.description: Striped legs, a giraffe's tongue, and a body science did not confirm existed until 1901. Spent the meantime being a rumour.

entries.title: Opossum
entries.description: The death act is involuntary and deeply committed. Largely immune to snake venom and carries almost no rabies, neither of which improves its reputation.

entries.title: Orca
entries.description: Apex of every ocean it enters, and the hunting method is taught rather than inherited. Each pod speaks with its own accent.

entries.title: Oryx
entries.description: Straight horns visible from a great distance, and a body that lets its own temperature climb rather than waste water on sweating.

entries.title: Otter
entries.description: Uses a rock as a tool and keeps a favourite one in a pocket of loose skin. Holds hands while sleeping so the current cannot separate them.

entries.title: Pangolin
entries.description: The only mammal wearing scales, rolled into a ball a lion cannot open. Trafficked more than any other mammal on earth, which the ball cannot solve.

entries.title: Peacock
entries.description: The train is not a tail and is grown fresh every year, purely so that somebody looks. Screams like a person in real distress.

entries.title: Peafowl
entries.description: Covers both the one everybody pictures and the one doing the choosing. She is the entire reason the display exists.

entries.title: Pika
entries.description: Refuses to hibernate. Spends all summer cutting and stacking hay instead, then lives inside the stack, squeaking about it continuously.

entries.title: Pufferfish
entries.description: Inflates into something unswallowable and carries a toxin with no antidote. Some of them draw enormous geometric circles in the sand to court.

entries.title: Puffin
entries.description: Carries a dozen fish crosswise in its beak without dropping any of them. Nests down a burrow. Flies as though it were thrown.

entries.title: Quokka
entries.description: The face reads as a smile and is simply the shape of the jaw. Approaches anyway, which is why the misunderstanding has lasted this long.

entries.title: Quoll
entries.description: A spotted marsupial predator that hunts after dark and has been losing badly to introduced cane toads it has no way to recognise as new.

entries.title: Raccoon
entries.description: Hands with genuine dexterity and no respect whatsoever for a latch. The washing is investigation, not hygiene.

entries.title: Seahorse
entries.description: The male carries the pregnancy. Anchors to weed with a prehensile tail and greets the same partner every single morning.

entries.title: Skunk
entries.description: Gives ample warning: stamps, raises the tail, and waits. What follows is entirely the fault of whoever ignored all three.

entries.title: Springhare
entries.description: A rodent that hops like a very small kangaroo and, under ultraviolet light, turns out to glow pink. Nobody knows why.

entries.title: Starfish
entries.description: Regrows from a fragment and everts its stomach to eat things where they sit. Has no brain and has never once needed one.

entries.title: Stingray
entries.description: Lies buried with only the eyes showing. The barb is purely defensive and the animal would much rather you had looked down.

entries.title: Tamandua
entries.description: A tree-going anteater with a tail that grips and claws that rule out a handshake. Smells strongly enough to be noticed first.

entries.title: Tapir
entries.description: A prehensile snout on a body essentially unchanged for twenty million years. Swims well and prefers to solve problems by going underwater.

entries.title: Tarantula
entries.description: Kicks irritating hairs off its own abdomen rather than bothering to bite. Molts by climbing out of itself entirely and waiting to harden.

entries.title: Tarsier
entries.description: Each eye is larger than its brain and cannot rotate, so the head turns almost the whole way around instead. Jumps forty times its own length.

entries.title: Toucan
entries.description: The beak is mostly air and works as a radiator. Lightweight, alarming, and better at reaching fruit than at anything else it attempts.

entries.title: Wallaby
entries.description: A kangaroo scaled down and correspondingly harder to spot. Boxes when required and would prefer not to be required.

entries.title: Weasel
entries.description: Long enough to follow prey down its own burrow, which is the whole strategy. Kills things considerably larger than itself as a matter of routine.

entries.title: Wolverine
entries.description: Twenty-five kilos that will contest a bear's kill and frequently win the argument. Covers distances that make no sense for its size.

entries.title: Wombat
entries.description: Produces cubed droppings and stacks them deliberately. Blocks its own burrow with a rump reinforced like a shield.

entries.title: Yak
entries.description: Built for air with very little in it. Provides wool, milk, transport and, once dried, the only fuel available at that altitude.

entries.title: Zebra
entries.description: The stripes appear to be about flies rather than lions, which is a considerably less dramatic answer than anybody wanted.
